prosody.lang: Look up: this dome has been floating here for fifteen centuries. Byzantine Emperor Justinian had this building finished at astonishing speed, in just five years. Legend says that on opening day he walked in, looked up at the dome and said, "Solomon, I have surpassed you", meaning the legendary Temple of Solomon in Jerusalem. For almost a thousand years it was the largest church in the world. When Sultan

the Conqueror took the city in 1453, he came straight here and turned it into a mosque. The minarets were added later. Under the Republic it became a museum; today it is a mosque again. Visitors tour the building from the upper gallery, which brings you much closer to the dome. Up there you see two worlds at once: Byzantine saints in gold mosaics, and below, giant round panels with names written in Arabic calligraphy. Look at the windows around the base of the dome. Light pours in there, so the dome seems to hang in the air instead of resting on stone. The Byzantines said the same thing: as if it were hung from heaven on a chain. In the south gallery, look for the Deësis mosaic: Christ with Mary and John the Baptist on either side. The faces still move people more than seven centuries on. Perhaps what has kept it standing so long is that every age has looked at it with the same awe.
